stem: Air temperature and RH are stable, but infrared measurements show leaves are several degrees cooler than the surrounding air. Why can an air-based VPD value misrepresent the leaf-level vapor-pressure gradient?
choices: Leaf temperature affects saturation vapor pressure at the leaf surface
Leaf temperature changes only nutrient EC
Air RH automatically becomes zero when leaves cool
Leaf temperature has no relationship to vapor pressure
rationale: Leaf-to-air vapor-pressure interpretation depends on leaf temperature as well as atmospheric moisture. A cooler leaf has a different saturation vapor pressure than the surrounding air.
